study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping Neurophysiological Subtypes of Major Depressive Disorder Using Normative Models of the Functional Connectome

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and methods clearly state objectives: to characterize lifespan trajectories of functional connectivity strength (FCS) using a normative model, quantify individual deviations in MDD, identify reproducible neurophysiological subtypes, and assess clinical relevance including treatment prediction. This directly states research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling (individual-level heterogeneity mapping, subtyping, and clinical prediction).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "First, we characterized typical lifespan trajectories of functional connectivity strength based on the normative model and quantitatively mapped the heterogeneous individual deviations among patients with MDD. Then, we identified neurobiological MDD subtypes... Finally, we validated the subtype differences in baseline clinical variables and longitudinal treatment predictive capacity."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This is a new normative model built from healthy controls (HCs). Eligibility criteria are described (HCs with no Axis I disorder; exclusion criteria listed). Image quality and data completeness standards are specified (motion thresholds, abnormal anatomy, incomplete coverage, TSNR). Final sample size and detailed reasons for exclusion are reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The HCs did not have a current or lifetime history of any Axis I disorder. The exclusion criteria for all participants included MRI contraindications, a history of drug or alcohol abuse... or any neurological disorders." | "Through strict quality control on clinical and imaging data, 187 participants were excluded due to... excessive head motion (exceeding 3 mm translational, 3° rotational or 0.5 mm mean FD, N=71), incomplete coverage (N=46), abnormalities in anatomical images (N=14), ..." | "Ultimately, 2,227 participants (1,148 patients with MDD and 1,079 HCs) were included in the analysis."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates age and sex are explicitly modeled in the normative model. Multi-site effects are addressed via ComBat harmonization on FCS values.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "For each brain region, we estimated a normative model of FCS as a function of age and sex by using Gaussian process regression (GPR)." | "Finally, combat [ComBat] harmonization was utilized to correct the site effects on the FCS values."
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: 1-s2.0-S0006322323013318-mmc1.pdf.md: Normative modeling for FCS; Data acquisition and preprocessing

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.location: 1-s2.0-S0006322323013318-mmc1.pdf.md: Data acquisition and preprocessing; Table S2

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software (SPM12, SeeCAT) and steps are described: discarding initial volumes, slice-timing and motion correction, normalization, resampling, smoothing, detrending, nuisance regression, bandpass filtering, and scrubbing with framewise displacement threshold.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The R-fMRI data were preprocessed using SPM12 ... and SeeCAT ... The first ten time points ... were discarded... slicetiming correction and head-motion correction... normalized... resampled to 3-mm... smoothed with a 6-mm ... Gaussian kernel, and linearly detrended. Several confounding covariates... were regressed... Temporal bandpass filtering (0.01-0.1 Hz) was further applied. Finally, a 'scrubbing' procedure ... volumes with framewise displacement exceeding 0.5 mm ... replaced with ... interpolated data."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They used a data partitioning strategy (10-fold cross-validation) on HCs to assess generalizability; models were trained on nine folds and tested on the held-out fold, repeated so each fold served as test once.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To assess the generalizability of the models, we first estimated the normative models in the HC group under 10-fold cross-validation... Nine folds ... used to train ... remaining fold ... to estimate generalization performance... repeated 10 times so that each fold was excluded once."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For a newly built normative model, external validation would require applying the model to an independent healthy dataset not used in model development. The study reports internal 10-fold cross-validation and then trains on all HCs, but does not apply the normative model to an independent external HC dataset.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "... 10-fold cross-validation ... We then trained the final normative models on the whole HC dataset for the subsequent MDD deviation analyses." (No mention of application to an external healthy dataset.)

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical model (Gaussian process regression) and covariates (age, sex) are specified, and the implementation software (PCNtoolkit) is named. However, key model settings such as kernel choice or priors are not detailed.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "For each brain region, we estimated a normative model of FCS as a function of age and sex by using Gaussian process regression (GPR)." | "The estimation of the normative models was performed using the PCNtoolkit package (https://github.com/amarquand/PCNtoolkit)."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Quantitative metrics assessing fit are reported from 10-fold CV on HCs: standardized mean squared error (SMSE) and mean squared log-loss (MSLL) with values, indicating good generalization.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "... overall standardized mean squared error close to 1 (0.996 ± 0.013) and a mean squared log-loss close to 0 (−0.001 ± 0.007) (Figure S2)."
